main_body: A loom frame: a wooden outer frame (brown beams) holding a cloth panel of white vertical warp threads with a red/yellow checker border, standing on two short legs. It is drawn flat, straight on.
top_band: rows 10-12 brown/tan (#b77246, #d59147) are the top beam of the frame, only 3 rows and the same tone family as the bottom beam and side posts. It reads as a front-facing beam, not a horizontal surface.
evidence: The column at x=16 reads: dark outline (row 9), brown beam rows 10-12, grey inner edge row 13, then the cloth/warp panel rows 14-21, then a bottom beam rows 22-24 in the same brown tones as the top, and an outline at row 25. The top beam and the bottom beam are mirror images of each other in the same tones, so the top beam is a vertical face, not a horizontal surface. The cloth panel is a vertical face. No horizontal top surface is visible on the beams, and the base shows no top face. The legs below are plain vertical posts. This matches the red front elevation example in the guide.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown (#411e05) that sits next to the wood, so it is tinted and not near-black (0% neutral edge pixels). The wood has about 4 steps (dark brown, mid brown, light brown, tan), and the cloth has a few more (white, grey, red, yellow), but the beams are flat bands with no grain. The checker border and the warp stripes give a pattern with no flat 5x5 fills (0%). The median of 11 colours per tile and 12 distinct colours is lower than the references at 17-20 per tile and 38-40 distinct colours, so it is thinner than the reference, with less texture on the wood and a repeated pattern doing most of the work. It does not reach the reference's richness, so it fails.
